why: This gate rejects retired commands and assets, not runtime/version vocabulary. Five representative mutations exercise disabled matching, substring exceptions, discarded findings, ignored enumeration/read floors and a global command bypass. They are not exhaustive parser proof.

mutations.name: command and asset patterns stop matching
mutations.breaks: Every retired command and content asset becomes clean even though files are still enumerated and read.

mutations.name: an exception matches by substring instead of exact line
mutations.breaks: Appending a second retired instruction to an exempted inert sample inherits its exception.
mutations.find: hit = exact.get((path, original[start].strip())) if len(block) == 1 else None
mutations.replace: hit = next((v for (p, t), v in exact.items() if p == path and t in original[start].strip()), None) if len(block) == 1 else None

mutations.name: findings are collected then reported clean
mutations.breaks: Correct matching never produces a failing exit; the real main-entry fixtures must reject it.
mutations.find:
if findings:
        for path, n, why in findings:

mutations.name: enumeration and read floors are ignored
mutations.breaks: Empty or shrunken enumeration and no readable known text receive a clean verdict.
